p: בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא, ב):
— In the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 11:2):
"בֵּרְכוֹ בְּאוֹר פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם וְכוּלֵי,
— “He blessed it with the light of a man’s face, etc.,
לֹא דוֹמֶה אוֹר פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם כָּל יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא דוֹמֶה בְּשַׁבָּת".
— the radiance of a man’s face throughout all the days of the year does not compare to what it resembles on Shabbat.”
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן נִבְרָא בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ,
— And this means that Adam the First was created in our divine image and after our likeness,
וְזֶה עִנְיָן שֶׁמַּזְכִּירִין בַּגְּמָרָא וְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
— and this is the concept cited in the Gemara and the holy Zohar:
"שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, דְּיַעֲקֹב הֲוָה שׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן" (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פד.),
— “The radiant beauty of Adam the First, that Jacob possessed the radiant beauty of Adam the First” (Bava Metzia 84a),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁצוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
— which explains what they taught: that the form of Jacob is engraved upon the Throne of Glory
דְּמוּת אָדָם שֶׁעַל הַכִּסֵּא.
— as the likeness of man upon the Throne.
וְאִיתָא (שָׁם בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה יא, ב):
— And it is brought (there in Bereishit Rabbah 11:2):
רַבָּנַן אָמְרֵי: בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת נִיטַּל זִיווֹ מִמֶּנּוּ וּטְרָדוֹ מִגַּן עֵדֶן,
— the Rabbis said: at the departure of Shabbat his celestial radiance was removed from him and He expelled him from the Garden of Eden,
"מְשַׁנֶּה פָנָיו וַתְּשַׁלְּחֵהוּ" (אִיּוֹב יד, כ),
— “You change his countenance and send him away” (Job 14:20),
וַהֲרֵי שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת הָיָה לוֹ הָאוֹר פָּנִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּבְרָא.
— proving that on Shabbat he retained the facial radiance exactly as he was created.

p: וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ קצא עַמּוּד א)
— And it is stated in the holy Zohar (in this Parashah, 191a)
דְּכָל זִמְנָא דְּבַר נָשׁ קָאֵים בְּעָלְמָא,
— that all the time man stands upright in the world,
כָּל אִינּוּן בִּרְיָין דְּעָלְמָא זָקְפִין רֵישָׁא וּמִסְתַּכְּלִין בִּדְיוֹקְנָא עִילָּאָה דְּבַר נָשׁ,
— all the creatures of the world lift their heads and gaze upon the supernal form of man,
כְּדֵין כּוּלְּהוּ דַּחֲלִין וְזָעִין מִקַּמֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵי,
— then they all revere and tremble before him, etc.,
וְהֵבִיא מִדָּנִיֵּאל, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— and it cites this from Daniel, see there.
וּמַסִּיק:
— And it concludes:
וְעַל דָּא מִבָּעֵי לֵיהּ לְבַר נָשׁ לְאִסְתַּמְּרָא אָרְחוֹי וּשְׁבִילוֹי
— And therefore a man must guard his ways and his paths
בְּגִין דְּלָא יֶחֱטֵי קַמֵּי מָארֵיהּ וְיִתְקַיֵּים בִּדְיוֹקְנָא דְּאָדָם.
— so that he does not sin before his Master and remains established in the divine image of Adam.
תָּא חֲזֵי, יְחֶזְקֵאל נָטַר פּוּמֵיהּ מִמַּאֲכָלֵי דְּאִיסּוּרֵי וְכוּלֵי,
— Come and see: Ezekiel guarded his mouth from forbidden foods, etc.,
זָכָה וְאִתְקְרֵי "בֶּן אָדָם";
— he merited and was titled “Son of Adam”;
דָּנִיֵּאל, מַה כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ?
— Daniel, what is written concerning him?
"אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִתְגָּאַל בְּפַת בַּג הַמֶּלֶךְ וּבְיֵין מִשְׁתָּיו" (דָּנִיֵּאל א, ח),
— “That he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's delicacies, nor with the wine which he drank” (Daniel 1:8),
זָכָה הוּא וְאִתְקַיֵּים בִּדְיוֹקְנֵיהּ דְּאָדָם וְכוּלֵי.
— he merited and was preserved in the pristine image of Adam, etc.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעִיקַּר הַתְחָלַת קִלְקוּל הַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה בַּאֲכִילָה,
— And this means that the core inception of the serpentine ruin was through eating,
וְלָכֵן מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה וּמְתַקֵּן אֲכִילָתוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
— and therefore whoever merits and sanctifies his eating to be in holiness
זוֹכֶה לִדְיוֹקְנָא דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל.
— merits the divine form of Adam the First prior to the fall.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל אֲכִילָתוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
— Therefore on Shabbat, when every single Jew eats in holiness,
זוֹכִין לִדְיוֹקְנָא דְּאָדָם,
— they merit the form of Adam,
וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "בֵּרְכוֹ בְּאוֹר פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם וְכוּלֵי",
— and this is what was stated: “He blessed it with the light of a man’s face, etc.,”
שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת זוֹכִין לְפָנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— for on Shabbat they merit new countenances, the image of Adam the First,
וְזֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "בְּרַם אַנְפִּין חֲדַתִּין וְכוּלֵי".
— and this is what we chant: “Truly new faces, etc.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 13:1: “Before the sin of Adam the First, his radiance and the features of his face outshone the orb of the sun, as the Midrash Rabbah states at the beginning of Acharei Mos. After the ruin his radiance was taken from him, as it says, ‘You change his countenance and send him away,’ except that the radiance remained with him until after Shabbat, as Bereishit Rabbah states there. So too for all generations, the facial radiance that a person merits on Shabbat remains: the light of a man’s face that he has on Shabbat does not resemble that of the weekdays. Although we now have no sign by which to recognize this, the masters of the Midrash understood it. … The Midrash uses two expressions for the facial radiance, ‘He blessed it’ and ‘He sanctified it,’ for a person attains the root of facial radiance in two ways: through the holiness of the wisdom of the holy Torah, as it is taught (Nedarim 49b), ‘…but the wisdom of a man illuminates his face’; and also through joy of heart, as it says, ‘A glad heart makes the face cheerful.’ ‘He sanctified it with the light of his face’ refers to the wisdom of man, for holiness is wisdom, as is known from the holy Zohar; and ‘He blessed it with the light of his face’ refers to joy of heart.”

p: וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם):
— And in the holy Zohar (there):
אָמַר רַבִּי חִזְקִיָּה: אִי הָכִי, הָא כְּתִיב:
— Rabbi Chizkiyah said: If so, behold it is written:
"אֱלָהַי שְׁלַח מַלְאֲכֵהּ וּסְגַר וְגוֹמֵר" (דָּנִיֵּאל ו, כג),
— “My God has sent His angel and has shut, etc.” (Daniel 6:23),
מַשְׁמָע דִּבְגִין מַלְאָכָא דְּאַסְגַּר לְפוּמַּיְיהוּ לָא אִתְחַבַּל!
— implying that on account of the angel who shut their mouths he was not harmed!
אָמַר לוֹ: דְּיוֹקְנֵיהּ דְּבַר נָשׁ זַכָּאָה אִיהוּ מַלְאָכָא מַמָּשׁ דִּסְגַר פּוּמָא וְכוּלֵי,
— He said to him: The form of a righteous man is itself a literal angel that shuts the mouth, etc.,
וּבְגִין כָּךְ "שְׁלַח מַלְאֲכֵהּ" –
— and for that reason “He sent His angel”—
הַהוּא דְּכָל דְּיוֹקְנִין דְּעָלְמָא מִתְחַקְּקָן בֵּיהּ
— that divine entity in which all forms of the world are engraved,
וְאִיהוּ אַתְקֵיף דְּיוֹקְנֵי בֵּי וְכוּלֵי.
— and He reinforced my image within me, etc.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, קסו עַמּוּד א) רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּשְׁלַח:
— And it is based on what is written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 166a) at the beginning of Parashat Vayishlach:
"מַלְאַךְ ה' סָבִיב" (תְּהִלִּים לד, ח) – דָּא שְׁכִינְתָּא וְכוּלֵי,
— “The angel of Hashem encamps round about” (Psalms 34:8)—this is the Shechinah, etc.,
וְעַל זֶה רָמַז הָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּפָרָשַׁת "הַמַּלְאָךְ הַגֹּאֵל" (בְּרֵאשִׁית מח, טז)
— and the Ramban of blessed memory hinted to this in Parashat HaMal’akh HaGoel (Genesis 48:16)
שֶׁכָּתַב: "וּלְכָךְ אָמַר 'בְּקֶרֶב הָאָרֶץ'", עַיֵּין שָׁם;
— where he wrote: “And therefore he said ‘in the midst of the earth,’” see there;
וְכֵן כָּתַב בְּפָרָשַׁת הָעֲקֵידָה (שָׁם כב, יב):
— and so he wrote in the parashah of the Akeidah (ibid. 22:12):
"וּמַלְאַךְ ה' הוּא הַמּוֹנֵעַ וְהַמַּבְטִיחַ, יִתְבָּרֵר בַּפָּסוּק 'הַמַּלְאָךְ הַגֹּאֵל'",
— “and the angel of Hashem is the one preventing and promising, as will be clarified on the verse ‘the angel who redeems,’”

p: וְזֶה הַמְכֻוָּון בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "מַלְאֲכֵהּ – הַהוּא דְּכָל דְּיוֹקְנִין דְּעָלְמָא מִתְחַקְּקָן בֵּיהּ",
— And this is the meaning of “His angel—the one in whom all forms of the world are engraved,”
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר (סִימָן נח):
— and it is based on what is written in Sefer HaBahir (section 58):
"וַיִּנָּפַשׁ" – שֶׁמִּשָּׁם פּוֹרְחִין כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת;
— “and He rested (vayinafash)”—for from there all souls fly forth;
שֶׁמִּמִּדַּת מַלְכוּת שֶׁהוּא צְרוֹר הַחַיִּים, שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— showing that from the attribute of Malchut which is the bundle of life, emerges the root of Israel’s souls;
וּכְתִיב: "חָכְמַת אָדָם תָּאִיר פָּנָיו" (קֹהֶלֶת ח, א),
— and it is written: “The wisdom of a man illuminates his face” (Ecclesiastes 8:1),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ חָכְמָה עִילָּאָה שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "כִּי ה' יִתֵּן חָכְמָה" (מִשְׁלֵי ב, ו),
— which means there is supernal Chokhmah concerning which it is stated: “For Hashem gives wisdom,”
וְיֵשׁ חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה – חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— and there is lower Chokhmah—the wisdom of Solomon, the Oral Torah,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "חָכְמַת אָדָם",
— and this is termed “the wisdom of man,”
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר "תָּאִיר פָּנָיו",
— and regarding this it is stated “illuminates his face,”
וְזֶהוּ מַלְכוּת: "פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ",
— and this is Malchut: “The mouth—we call it the Oral Torah,”
שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְהָאוֹר פָּנִים.
— whence is the root of the souls of Israel and the facial radiance.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּדָנִיֵּאל שֶׁמָּצִינוּ דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: "וְחָכְמָה כְּחָכְמַת אֱלָהִין הִשְׁתְּכַחַת בֵּיהּ" (דָּנִיֵּאל ה, יא),
— Therefore with Daniel concerning whom we find it written: “and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods was found in him” (Daniel 5:11),
וּכְתִיב: "הִנֵּה חָכָם אַתָּה מִדָּנִיאֵל" (יְחֶזְקֵאל כח, ג);
— and it is written: “Behold you are wiser than Daniel” (Ezekiel 28:3);
וְכֵן בִּיחֶזְקֵאל אִיתָא (בְּרָכוֹת נז:):
— and so too regarding Ezekiel it is brought in Berakhot (57b):
"יְחֶזְקֵאל יְצַפֶּה לְחָכְמָה",
— “One who sees Ezekiel in a dream should anticipate wisdom,”
וְהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיְּחֶזְקֵאל גִּילָּה סִתְרֵי הַמֶּרְכָּבָה
— and that is because Ezekiel revealed the esoteric mysteries of the Divine Chariot
שֶׁהֵם דְּבָרִים שֶׁכִּיסָּה עַתִּיק יוֹמִין,
— which are secrets that the Ancient of Days had concealed,
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה,
— and this is the very root of Chokhmah;
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכֵי זָכוּ יְחֶזְקֵאל וְדָנִיֵּאל לִדְיוֹקְנָא דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— and on that account Ezekiel and Daniel merited the divine image of Adam the First,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ "חָכְמַת אָדָם תָּאִיר פָּנָיו".
— which is “The wisdom of a man illuminates his face.”

p: וּבְשַׁבָּת שֶׁזּוֹכֶה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי לִנְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה,
— And on Shabbat when every Jew merits an additional soul (neshamah yeteirah),
שֶׁאַף שֶׁבַּפָּסוּק נִרְמַז: "וַיִּנָּפַשׁ" – וַוי שֶׁאָבְדָה נֶפֶשׁ,
— wherein although in the verse it is hinted: “vayinafash”—woe that a soul is departed,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַלָּשׁוֹן בַּגְּמָרָא (בֵּיצָה טז.): "נְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה נוֹתֵן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּאָדָם עַרְבֵי שַׁבָּתוֹת וְכוּלֵי".
— nevertheless the Talmudic formulation in Beitzah (16a) is: “An additional soul the Holy One, blessed be He, places in a man on the eve of Shabbat, etc.”
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר הַלָּשׁוֹן "וַוי שֶׁאָבְדָה נֶפֶשׁ",
— And that which it phrased “woe that a soul is departed”,
בֵּיאֵר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, רד עַמּוּד ב):
— it was elucidated in the holy Zohar (Part II, 204b):
הַהוּא רוּחָא שַׁרְיָא בְּגַוַּוהּ דְּהַהִיא נֶפֶשׁ וְכוּלֵי,
— that supernal spirit rests within that very soul, etc.,
וּכְדֵין הַהִיא נֶפֶשׁ יְתֵירָה בְּרִבּוּיָא וְתוֹעַלְתָּא יַתִּיר מִמַּה דַּהֲוָה וְכוּלֵי,
— and then that soul is enhanced with vast abundance and utility far beyond what it was previously, etc.,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַנֶּפֶשׁ זוֹכָה לִנְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה.
— meaning that the lower soul is elevated to receive the additional neshamah.
וְכֵן הַלָּשׁוֹן בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם פח עַמּוּד ב):
— And so is the language in the holy Zohar (ibid. 88b):
"בְּשַׁבַּתָּא יָהֲבִין לֵיהּ לְבַר נָשׁ נִשְׁמָתָא אָחֳרָא,
— “On Shabbat they bestow upon a man another soul,
נִשְׁמָתָא עִילָּאָה, נִשְׁמָתָא דְּכָל שְׁלִימוּ בָּהּ וְכוּלֵי",
— a supernal soul, a soul containing all perfection, etc.”
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "בְּרַם אַנְפִּין חֲדַתִּין, וְרוּחִין עִם נַפְשִׁין".
— and this is what we chant: “Truly new faces, and spirits with souls.”

paragraphs.text: Beitzah 16a: “As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, gives a person an additional soul on Shabbat eve, and at the conclusion of Shabbat removes it from him, as it is stated: ‘He ceased from work and was refreshed (vayinafash)’ (Exodus 31:17). Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish expounds the verse as follows: Since he ceased from work, and now Shabbat has concluded and his additional soul is removed from him, woe (vai) for the additional soul (nefesh) that is lost.”

p: וְזֶה זוֹכִין בִּסְעוּדָה דִּמְעַלֵּי שַׁבַּתָּא,
— And this they merit at the Friday night meal,
סְעוּדָתָא דַּחֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין,
— the meal of the Field of Holy Apples,
שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל "תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין" כְּמוֹ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
— for Israel were termed “holy apples” just as at the Giving of the Torah,
שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְתַפּוּחַ כְּשֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ "נַעֲשֶׂה" לְ"נִשְׁמַע"
— wherein Israel were compared to an apple tree when they prioritized “we will do” before “we will hear”
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שַׁבָּת פח.),
— (as written in Shabbat 88a),
וְאָמַר שָׁם: מִי גִּלָּה לְבָנַי רָז זֶה שֶׁמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁין בּוֹ,
— and Hashem said there: “Who revealed to My children this secret that the ministering angels use?”
דִּכְתִיב: "בָּרְכוּ ה' מַלְאָכָיו גִּבֹּרֵי כֹחַ עֹשֵׂי דְבָרוֹ לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹל דְּבָרוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים קג, כ) –
— as it is written: “Bless Hashem, His angels, mighty in strength, that do His word, hearkening unto the voice of His word” (Psalms 103:20) –
בְּרֵישָׁא "עֹשֵׂי" וַהֲדַר "לִשְׁמֹעַ".
— first “that do” and afterward “hearkening”.
"דִּבּוּר" הַיְינוּ מִדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה,
— “Word/Speech” denotes the final attribute (Malchut),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם קלח:):
— and as written (there, 138b):
"דְּבַר ה'" – זוֹ הֲלָכָה,
— “The word of Hashem”—this is Halakhah,
וְהַיְינוּ: מַלְכוּת פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ.
— which is: Malchut is the mouth, we title it the Oral Torah.
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, לב עַמּוּד א):
— And in the holy Zohar (Part I, 32a):
"וְהַאי דִּבּוּר אִיקְרֵי שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי",
— “And this speech is called Shabbat, etc.,”
וּכְתִיב: "לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹל דְּבָרוֹ",
— and it is written: “hearkening unto the voice of His word,”
שֶׁהַקּוֹל הוּא חַיּוּת הַדִּבּוּר,
— for the voice is the animating vitality of the word,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, ג עַמּוּד א):
— and as written (Zohar Part II, 3a):
"קוֹל אָתֵי לְדִבּוּר וּמְדַבֵּר לָהּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ",
— “The voice arrives unto the word and leads it along with it,”
וְזֶהוּ "לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹל דְּבָרוֹ".
— and this is “hearkening unto the voice of His word.”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 88a: “Rabbi Elazar said: When the Jewish people accorded precedence to the declaration ‘We will do’ over ‘We will hear,’ a Divine Voice emerged and said to them: Who revealed to my children this secret that the ministering angels use? As it is written: ‘Bless the Lord, you angels of His, you mighty in strength, that fulfill His word, hearkening unto the voice of His word’ (Psalms 103:20). At first, the angels fulfill His word, and then afterward they hearken. Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: What is the meaning of that which is written: ‘As an apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. Under its shadow I delighted to sit and its fruit was sweet to my taste’ (Song of Songs 2:3)? Why were the Jewish people likened to an apple tree? It is to tell you that just as this apple tree, its fruit grows before its leaves, so too, the Jewish people accorded precedence to ‘We will do’ over ‘We will hear.’”

p: וּכְתִיב "עֹשֵׂי דְבָרוֹ" עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, קכג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב):
— And it is written “that do His word” based on what is stated in the holy Zohar (Part III, 123b):
הַתּוֹרָה וְהַמִּצְוָה דְּאִינּוּן בֵּן וּבַת,
— the Torah and the commandment which are son and daughter,
וְזֶה וָא"ו הֵ"א,
— and this represents the letters Vav and Hei of the Tetragrammaton,
הֵ"א אַחֲרוֹנָה מִדַּת מַלְכוּת,
— the final Hei being the attribute of Malchut,
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "עֹשֵׂי דְבָרוֹ" –
— and this is what Scripture states: “that do His word”—
שֶׁהַמִּצְוָה בָּאָה מִמִּדַּת מַלְכוּת שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת "דְּבָרוֹ";
— for the practical commandment stems from Malchut which is termed “His word”;
"לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹל דְּבָרוֹ" –
— “hearkening unto the voice of His word”—
קוֹל שֶׁהוּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
— voice which represents the Holy One, blessed be He (Zeir Anpin / Tiferet),
קוֹל חַיּוּת הַדִּבּוּר.
— the vocal vitality of the spoken word.
וְעַל כֵּן סִדֵּר הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
— Therefore the holy Ari of blessed memory established
סְעוּדָתָא דִּמְעַלֵּי שַׁבָּתָא נֶגֶד קְדוּשַׁת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— the Friday night meal to align with the holiness of our father Isaac, peace be upon him,
וְעַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ קפט עַמּוּד ב):
— and based on what is written in the holy Zohar (in this Parashah, 189b):
"וְאִלֵּין בְּנֵי נָשָׁא דְּאִתְתַּקְּפוּ עֲלֵיהּ אִקְרוּן גִּבּוֹרֵי כֹחַ וְכוּלֵי,
— “And those people who fortified themselves over it are called mighty in strength, etc.,
וְאִלֵּין מַלְאָכָיו דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא דְּאָתְיָין מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה קַשְׁיָא וְכוּלֵי".
— and these are the angels of the Holy One, blessed be He, who emerge from the side of stern Gevurah, etc.”
וְכֵן בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ לְהַלָּן (קצב סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) דָּרַשׁ:
— And likewise in the holy Zohar further on (192b end) it expounded:
"וַה' נָתַן קוֹלוֹ" (יוֹאֵל ב, יא) – דָּא הוּא קָלָא דִּכְתִיב: "קוֹל דְּבָרִים וְכוּלֵי",
— “And Hashem uttered His voice” (Joel 2:11)—this is the supernal voice concerning which it is written: “the voice of words, etc.,”
וְהַיְינוּ קוֹל דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
— meaning the cosmic voice of the Giving of the Torah.
וּכְתִיב: "כִּי עָצוּם עֹשֵׂה דְבָרוֹ" (שָׁם),
— And it is written: “For strong is he that executes His word” (ibid.),
וְ"עָצוּם" וְ"גִּבֹּרֵי כֹחַ" הוּא מִדַּת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם – פַּחַד יִצְחָק.
— and “strong” and “mighty in strength” characterize the attribute of our father Isaac, peace be upon him—the Dread of Isaac (Pachad Yitzchak).
וְלָכֵן בִּמְעַלֵּי שַׁבָּתָא, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מַשִּׂיג הַפַּחַד וְהַיִּרְאָה,
— Therefore on Friday night, when every single Jew attains holy fear and reverence,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (פֶּרֶק ד דִּדְמַאי הֲלָכָה א):
— and as written in the Yerushalmi (Demai 4:1):
"אֵימַת שַׁבָּת עַל עַם הָאָרֶץ",
— “The dread of Shabbat rests upon even an unlearned person (am ha-aretz),”
וְזֶה מוֹעִיל דְּנֶאֱמָן תֵּיכֶף בִּכְנִיסַת שַׁבָּת,
— and this is effective so that he is believed immediately upon the entry of Shabbat,
נִקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל "תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין" כְּמוֹ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
— Israel are termed “holy apples” just as at the Giving of the Torah.

p: וּבְשַׁבָּת כָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ מַחֲזִיר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הַכְּתָרִים,
— And on Shabbat the holy Ari of blessed memory wrote that Moses our teacher restores to Israel the crowns,
וְהַיְינוּ הַשְּׁנֵי כְּתָרִים: אֶחָד כְּנֶגֶד "נַעֲשֶׂה" וְאֶחָד כְּנֶגֶד "נִשְׁמָע",
— namely the two crowns: one corresponding to “we will do” and one corresponding to “we will hear,”
שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶם אָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת פח.):
— concerning which they taught in the Gemara (Shabbat 88a):
"וְכוּלָּם זָכָה מֹשֶׁה וּנְטָלָן",
— “and all of them Moses merited and took,”
וּמֵהֶם זָכָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לְאוֹר פָּנִים,
— and from these Moses our teacher merited facial radiance,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי קָרַן עוֹר פָּנָיו" (שְׁמוֹת לד, כט)
— as it is stated: “that the skin of his face shone” (Exodus 34:29)
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת.
— and as Tosafot wrote.
וּבְשַׁבָּת, כְּשֶׁמַּחֲזִיר הַכְּתָרִים לְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
— And on Shabbat, when he restores these crowns to every single Jew,
זוֹכִין לְאוֹר פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם,
— they merit the radiance of the face of Adam,
וְזֶהוּ "בֵּרְכוֹ בְּאוֹר פָּנָיו וְכוּלֵי",
— and this is “He blessed it with the light of a man’s face, etc.,”
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "בְּרַם אַנְפִּין חֲדַתִּין וְרוּחִין".
— and this is what we chant: “Truly new faces and spirits.”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 88a: “Rabbi Simai taught: When Israel accorded precedence to the declaration ‘We will do’ over the declaration ‘We will hear,’ 600,000 ministering angels came and tied two crowns to each and every member of the Jewish people, one corresponding to ‘We will do’ and one corresponding to ‘We will hear.’ And when the people sinned with the Golden Calf, 1,200,000 angels of destruction descended and removed them from the people, as it is stated in the wake of the sin of the Golden Calf: ‘And the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward’ (Exodus 33:6). Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: At Horeb they put on their ornaments, and at Horeb they removed them. The source for this is: At Horeb they put them on, as we have said; at Horeb they removed them, as it is written: ‘And the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb.’ Rabbi Yoḥanan said: And Moses merited all of these crowns and took them. What is the source for this? Because juxtaposed to this verse, it is stated: ‘And Moses would take the tent (ohel)’ (Exodus 33:7). The word ohel is interpreted homiletically as an allusion to an aura or illumination (hila). Reish Lakish said: In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will return them to us, as it is stated: ‘And the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come with singing unto Zion, and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads’ (Isaiah 35:10). The joy that they once had will once again be upon their heads.”

p: גַּם אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, מז עַמּוּד ב):
— Also it is brought in the holy Zohar (Part I, 47b):
"בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי" – דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה דְּאִיהוּ יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי וְכוּלֵי,
— “On the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah which is the seventh day, etc.,
דְּשַׁבָּת מִדַּת מַלְכוּת: "פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה",
— for Shabbat is the attribute of Malchut: “The mouth, the Oral Torah,”
וְאָז הַזְּמַן לִזְכּוֹת לְאוֹר פָּנִים כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "חָכְמַת אָדָם תָּאִיר פָּנָיו",
— and then is the auspicious time to merit facial radiance as it is stated: “The wisdom of a man illuminates his face,”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁהוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת "חָכְמַת אָדָם",
— and as we noted, this is the Oral Torah which is termed “the wisdom of man,”
וְזֶהוּ "אַנְפִּין חֲדַתִּין וְרוּחִין עִם נַפְשִׁין" שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד.
— and this is “new faces and spirits with souls” which are unified as one.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אוֹמְרִים: "לְמֶעְבַּד נִשְׁמָתִין וְרוּחִין חֲדַתִּין".
— And subsequently we chant: “To fashion new souls and spirits.”
וּבִסְעוּדָה זוֹ מַשִּׂיגִין הַיִּרְאָה פַּחַד יִצְחָק,
— And during this meal one attains reverence, the Dread of Isaac,
זוֹכִין לְאוֹר פָּנִים שֶׁכָּל הָאֲכִילוֹת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
— meriting facial radiance through all foods being consumed in sanctity,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה זוֹכִין לְאוֹר פָּנִים וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
— from which one merits facial radiance as we said.

p: וּבֶאֱמֶת תָּלוּי זֶה בָּזֶה,
— And in truth these two dimensions depend upon one another,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי אֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה זוֹכִין לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
— for through eating in sanctity one merits words of Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ בְּתוֹסָפוֹת (כְּתוּבּוֹת קד. דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל 'לֹא') בְּשֵׁם מִדְרָשׁ:
— and as written in Tosafot (Ketubot 104a) citing a Midrash:
עַד שֶׁאָדָם יִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁיִּכָּנְסוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְתוֹךְ גּוּפוֹ,
— “Before a person prays that words of Torah should enter into his body,
יִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנְסוּ מַעֲדַנִּים לְתוֹךְ גּוּפוֹ,
— let him pray that delicacies should not enter into his body,”
וּכְעֵין זֶה אִיתָא בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כו).
— and similar to this is brought in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu (Seder Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 26).
וְכֵן עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה זוֹכִין שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הָאֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
— And likewise through words of Torah one merits that his physical eating be elevated in sanctity,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, קכד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב):
— and as written in the holy Zohar (Part III, 124b end):
חֲכָמִים דְּדָמְיָין לְשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים
— scholars who are comparable to Sabbaths and Festivals
וַאֲכִילָתָם תָּמִיד בִּקְדוּשָּׁה כְּמוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת וְיוֹם טוֹב.
— and their eating is continuously in holiness like on Shabbat and Yom Tov.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ רַבִּי שֶׁאָמַר (כְּתוּבּוֹת קד.):
— And this is like Rebbe (Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi) who said (Ketubot 104a):
"וְלֹא נֶהֱנֵיתִי אֲפִילּוּ בְּאֶצְבַּע קְטַנָּה",
— “And I did not derive physical pleasure even with my smallest finger,”
וְהַתּוֹסָפוֹת (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יא. דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל 'צְנוֹן') הִקְשׁוּ מִזֶּה
— and Tosafot (Avodah Zarah 11a) challenged this
עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: שֶׁלֹּא פָּסְקוּ מֵעַל שֻׁלְחָנָם לֹא חַזֶּרֶת וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— from what the Gemara stated: that neither radish nor lettuce ever ceased from his table, etc., see there.
אַךְ יֵשׁ לְיַישֵׁב,
— However, one can resolve this:
שֶׁהוּא לֹא נֶהֱנָה כְּלָל מֵאֲכִילָתוֹ
— that he derived no self-serving pleasure whatsoever from his food,
שֶׁלֹּא הִרְגִּישׁ הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף,
— not feeling physical gratification at all,
רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לד, ג)
— rather in the manner of what is written (Vayikra Rabbah 34:3)
בְּהִלֵּל שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁהוֹלֵךְ לִגְמוֹל חֶסֶד עִם הָדֵין אַכְסַנְיָא בְּגַו בֵּיתָא וְכוּלֵי,
— concerning Hillel who said he was going to perform kindness with this guest inside the house, etc.,
"וְהָדֵין נַפְשָׁא עֲלוּבְתָא לָאו אַכְסַנְיָא הוּא בְּגַו גּוּפָא?",
— “and is not this impoverished soul merely a temporary guest within the physical body?”
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הִרְגִּישׁוּ כְּלָל הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף
— meaning that they did not feel bodily gratification at all,
רַק כְּגוֹמֵל חֶסֶד עִם אַכְסַנְיָא,
— rather solely like one performing kindness with a lodging guest,
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁאָמַר: "וְלֹא נֶהֱנֵיתִי וְכוּלֵי".
— and this is what Rebbe meant by: “And I did not derive physical pleasure, etc.”

p: וְהוּא כְּמוֹ אֲכִילַת שַׁבָּת וְיוֹם טוֹב,
— And it is precisely like eating on Shabbat and Yom Tov,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת",
— and as we noted on the phrase “Whoever delights in the Sabbath,”
שֶׁהַמְכֻוָּון הוּא רַק לְעַנֵּג אֶת הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת "שַׁבָּת"
— that the true intent is solely to delight the additional soul which is titled “Shabbat”,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
— as written in the holy Zohar.
וּבְשַׁבָּת שֶׁזּוֹכִין לְרִיבּוּי הַשְׁפָּעָה בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
— And on Shabbat when we merit an abundant influx in the Oral Torah
וְגַם כָּל הָאֲכִילוֹת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
— and all foods are likewise consumed in holiness,
זוֹכִין לְתַקֵּן קִלְקוּל הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בַּאֲכִילָה
— we merit to rectify the serpentine ruin that occurred through eating
וְזוֹכִין לְאוֹר פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם,
— and we merit the radiant light of the face of Adam,
וְזֶהוּ "אַנְפִּין חֲדַתִּין".
— and this is “new countenances.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 6:1: “From the beginning of Creation there was also the evil inclination, as it says, ‘I created the evil inclination’ (Kiddushin 30b). Even before the ruin, Adam the First had this capacity, that the serpent could seduce him and bring desire into him. The serpent’s first seduction was through eating. Afterwards he cast filth into Chavah, and from this the filth came into Adam the First and his offspring; this too is called eating, as it says, ‘She ate and wiped her mouth.’ The Shabbat meal is a rectification for the blemish of eating, for the Shabbat meal is called ‘the meal of the King,’ which is like eating sacrifices, in holiness, just as with the eating of a Torah scholar, where one who feeds him is as though he offered the daily offerings (Berakhot 10b). This is the essence of the rectification: that one’s eating be in holiness, and through this one merits all holiness. … The eating of a Torah scholar is like words of Torah themselves, and we have already said that the eating of Shabbat is the eating of a Torah scholar. For the additional soul, which is called Shabbat, as the holy Zohar says, is with every Jew like a Torah scholar hosted in his house, and the Shabbat meal is like offering the daily offerings and pouring wine upon the altar.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Miketz 6 likewise sees the Shabbat meal as the repair of the serpent’s first damage, which began with eating. It adds why the meal has this power: the additional soul makes every Jew’s Shabbat meal the eating of a Torah scholar, akin to sacrifices. This joins the two themes Rav Tzadok links here, eating in holiness and the Oral Torah.
